title: Quiz: CRISP-DM and Setting Up the Course Dataset

questions.text: Which CRISP-DM phase is concerned with translating a business goal into a measurable data mining objective?
questions.explanation: Business Understanding (Phase 1) is where you define what the business wants to achieve and then convert that goal into a specific, measurable mining objective — for example, 'build a classifier with recall ≥ 0.70 for churn prediction'.

questions.text: Empirically, which CRISP-DM phase typically consumes the most project time?
questions.explanation: Data Preparation routinely consumes 60–70% of project time in practice. Cleaning missing values, resolving inconsistencies, encoding categoricals, and engineering features are labour-intensive even with good tooling.

questions.text: In sparklyr, what does the collect() function do?
options: Sends R data frames to Spark memory
Brings a Spark computation result back to an R tibble
Saves Spark output to a CSV file on HDFS
questions.explanation: collect() materialises a lazy Spark computation and returns the result as a local R tibble. You should only collect() small result sets (summaries, aggregations) — never collect() millions of raw rows unnecessarily.

questions.text: A fraud detection model achieves 97% accuracy on the test set. The fraud prevalence in that set is 3%. What is the most likely explanation?
options: The model has learned meaningful patterns in the data
The model always predicts 'not fraud' and achieves 97% by guessing the majority class
97% accuracy is too low for a fraud model; the model has failed
The model is overfitting the training data
questions.explanation: When fraud prevalence is 3%, a classifier that always predicts 'not fraud' achieves 97% accuracy without detecting a single fraudulent claim. This is the accuracy paradox. Precision and recall on the minority class are the appropriate metrics.

questions.text: In CRISP-DM, once you reach the Deployment phase you do not need to revisit earlier phases.
questions.explanation: CRISP-DM is explicitly circular. After deployment, model performance drifts as the world changes, new data quality issues emerge, and business goals evolve — all of which require cycling back to earlier phases.

questions.text: In the simulate_bdat602() dataset, which column is the primary continuous regression target?
questions.explanation: claim_amount is the primary continuous regression target, designed to have strong, interpretable signal from age, chronic conditions, BMI, smoker status, and plan tier. churned and high_risk are binary classification targets.
